decision: Correct future visible-text oracle only; preserve the frozen run5 failed verification unchanged.

source_evidence.claim: Section4.5 requires original visible words/punctuation in English double quotes without a once-per-prompt limit.
H2 checks quoted exact words are present; no occurrence equality.
Caller-provided sign lettering rendered in prose is obedience, not unlicensed addition.
The test expressly permits the same utterance in prose and its dialogue block without turning its echo into screen lettering.
User words in speech/visible text are excluded from media citation inference.

actual_case.reason: The shot-one description and host-rendered visible_text event refer to the same hanging sign. Shot two ends with only tile, pillars and the track edge visible, without its readable sign.

future_oracle.changes: Remove global final-prompt occurrence count for visible text; keep exact typed event multiplicity/word bytes and independently supplied authorized shot list. Require exact words present in quoted rendered channel. No dialogue checks changed.
future_oracle.selftest: same object/same shot description plus one typed event is accepted; duplicated event, altered bytes, forbidden-shot event, extra typed words and omitted quoted words are rejected.

semantic_controls.description: Two distinct readable signs in the same shot, represented by one typed event
semantic_controls.coverage: Independent artifact/semantic review; one shared shot is not a display-identity proof.

semantic_controls.description: A readable sign continues into an unauthorized second shot with no second event
semantic_controls.coverage: Existing visible_text_placement_mismatch semantic critic and independent review; event list alone is insufficient.

semantic_controls.description: The same overhead sign is described twice in shot one and has one exact typed display event, with its face excluded from shot two
semantic_controls.coverage: The present round5 artifact, not a general exemption for all repeated strings.

limitations: This correction distinguishes descriptions from physical displays. It does not prove generated-video text occurrence, and the old stricter assertion is not relabeled as having passed.
